category_title: First-grade students who struggle with independent literacy tasks and prefer social or auditory reading
minimal_context: The student is at a workstation during independent work time, tasked with writing a text-to-text connection to their book in their journal.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please sit at your workstation and write a connection to your book in your journal.

STUDENT: (Stares at the blank journal page) I don't know how to write it by myself.

TUTOR: Just think about what the book reminds you of and write it down.

STUDENT: (Puts the pencil down and looks around the room) Can I just tell my partner about the book instead?

TUTOR: No, this is independent work time. You need to write your connection.

STUDENT: (Pushes the journal away, completely off-task, and starts playing with a shoelace instead of attempting to share the text-to-text connection.) I can't write it.

options.A: Ensure the student receives no attention during independent work time to avoid reinforcing the off-task behavior.
options.B: Modify the assignment and ask the student to draw a picture of their connection in the journal.
options.C: Sit with the student one-on-one at the workstation to provide direct support for the writing task.
options.D: Allow or encourage the student to engage in physical activity to regulate their energy during the task.
